speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent; can you describe the rash on your scalp and forehead, including when it first appeared and what it looks like? Also, are you experiencing any itching, pain, or other symptoms along with it?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash appear greasy with yellowish scales, particularly in the hairline and behind the ears? Additionally, does the baby seem uncomfortable or scratch at the area, or is he otherwise content?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the greasy yellow scales on a 3-month-old, this sounds very much like cradle cap, or seborrheic dermatitis. I don't believe I need any further tests or images to confirm this at this time. DIAGNOSIS READY: Seborrheic Dermatitis
